implementation: DIRECT=1 scoped revision read transaction + 1 write transaction with scoped re-read; SOURCE=1 scoped revision read transaction + source outside transactions + 1 write transaction with scoped re-read; both share the atomic pending request/proposal/event seam

rows.probe: direct submission of a caller-supplied candidate: returned type, value shape and id prefix
rows.note: A direct call on a real ledger returned the generated proposal identifier, whose prefix and 32-hex suffix matched the persisted row.

rows.probe: direct submission durable footprint: per-table row-count delta across every table in the schema
rows.note: Full counts over every non-SQLite-internal schema table were sampled before and after one direct submission on the same ledger.

rows.probe: direct submission event: kind, subject_type, subject_id and the exact payload keys
rows.note: The newest real event row was decoded after direct submission and compared to the returned proposal identifier and exact payload key set.

rows.probe: direct request row shape: status, proposal_id, lease_owner, lease_until_us, attempts, operation_revision
rows.note: The request row bound to the returned proposal was read directly from SQLite and every requested lifecycle field was recorded.

rows.probe: direct submission while a configured candidate_source raises: source invocation count and the result
rows.note: A configured source that would raise remained uncalled while the caller-supplied candidate was persisted and returned normally.

rows.probe: direct proposals row: output and provenance text plus digests, status, and the status_sequence binding
rows.note: The proposal row and its audit event were read from SQLite; both canonical texts, both digests, status, and shared sequence were measured.

rows.probe: source-backed submission: returned type, and the footprint compared with Q02 after id normalization
rows.note: Separate real ledgers persisted byte-identical candidates through each public path; complete normalized request, proposal, event, and table deltas matched.

rows.probe: source-backed submission: source invocation count and every field of the CandidateRequest handed over
rows.note: The configured source retained the exact CandidateRequest from one real call, and its generated request identifier was matched to SQLite storage.

rows.probe: connection.in_transaction observed on every Cement-held connection while the source executes
rows.note: A Connection subclass delayed physical close so every Cement-created connection remained inspectable; all were out of transaction during source execution, while a live read block proved True.

rows.probe: the source raises CandidateSourceError: public class, message, __cause__, __context__ and frames
rows.note: A declared CandidateSourceError carrying a planted secret was raised through a real source call; the public exception and traceback were captured directly.

rows.probe: the source raises an arbitrary Exception carrying a planted secret: same observations, secret absent
rows.note: A RuntimeError carrying a planted secret crossed the real adapter boundary; class, text, chaining, frames, repr, and formatted traceback were captured.

rows.probe: propose with candidate_source None: class, message and source invocation count
rows.note: A real initialized System with candidate_source=None rejected the call after argument validation and before opening any ledger transaction.

rows.probe: the source returns a non-Candidate or a malformed provenance: class and exact message
rows.note: Two separate real ledgers measured a non-Candidate return and an object-valued provenance; both adapter result defects normalized identically.

rows.probe: the operation revision changes between generation and the write: class, message and durable footprint

observation.message: operation revision changed before proposal submission

rows.note: The real source committed an operation revision during generation; the locked recheck rejected revision one and persisted no submission rows or proposal event.

rows.probe: a bad partition together with a bad input_value: which error is reported

observation.direct_message: partition must be 1-128 ASCII letters, digits, '.', '_', ':', '/', or '-'
observation.source_backed_message: partition must be 1-128 ASCII letters, digits, '.', '_', ':', '/', or '-'

rows.note: Two live calls combined an invalid partition with a non-JSON input; both rejected the partition first.

rows.probe: a bad operation together with a bad input_value: which error is reported

observation.direct_message: operation must be 1-128 ASCII letters, digits, '.', '_', ':', '/', or '-'
observation.source_backed_message: operation must be 1-128 ASCII letters, digits, '.', '_', ':', '/', or '-'

rows.note: Two live calls combined an invalid operation with a non-JSON input; both rejected the operation first.

rows.probe: a bad partition together with an unregistered operation: which error, and transaction count

observation.message: partition must be 1-128 ASCII letters, digits, '.', '_', ':', '/', or '-'

rows.note: A live transaction wrapper and source counter showed that partition validation rejected the combined call before either capability ran.

rows.probe: a rejected call: transaction count and source invocation count, each with a positive control

observation.rejected_message: value of type 'object' is not JSON

rows.note: The rejected call recorded zero transactions and source calls; an immediate valid call proved both counters live with one read, one write, and one source call.

rows.probe: submit_proposal called without the candidate keyword: exact TypeError text
rows.note: A bound System method on a real initialized ledger produced Python's native missing-keyword-only TypeError.

rows.probe: source= passed to submit_proposal and to propose: exact TypeError text for each

observation.submit_message: System.submit_proposal() got an unexpected keyword argument 'source'
observation.propose_message: System.propose() got an unexpected keyword argument 'source'

rows.note: Both bound methods rejected source= through Python's native signature handling before the configured source could run.

rows.probe: unregistered operation on the source path: class, message, and whether the source ran

observation.message: operation is not registered in this partition

rows.note: A scoped read on an empty real ledger raised NotFoundError before source execution; registering the sibling operation then proved the source counter live.

rows.probe: a failed submission: ledger sha256, full iterdump, row counts and the event sequence counter
rows.note: Before and after one real failing source call, the physical file, complete iterdump tuple, all table counts, and sqlite_sequence event counter were independently sampled.

rows.probe: commit() call count on every failure path through a Connection-subclass factory, with a positive control
rows.note: A sqlite3.Connection subclass counted actual commit() dispatches across eight independent failure families; a no-op write transaction proved the spy with one call.

rows.probe: clock reads during a successful submission: self._now call count and any other clock consulted
rows.note: Wrapped self._now, the injected clock, and system_module.time.time_ns were counted independently for one successful call through each public path.

rows.probe: every SELECT executed during a successful submission, by table

selects.sql: SELECT revision FROM operations WHERE partition = ? AND name = ?
SELECT revision FROM operations WHERE partition = ? AND name = ?

rows.note: A Connection subclass captured every explicit SELECT template and bind tuple after setup was reset; one real source-backed success produced the recorded list.

rows.probe: the submitted proposal seen through get_proposal, proposal, proposals and function_report
rows.note: Four unchanged read APIs were called against the same submitted row; every projected proposal and request identity was compared, including FunctionReport's pending gap.

rows.probe: review accepting a submitted proposal, then compile and promote, end to end
rows.note: Two submitted proposals were accepted into real examples, then compiled, verified, promoted, and consumed through unchanged handle as an artifact resolution.

rows.probe: byte-identical content submitted twice: proposal ids, request rows, events and any conflict
rows.note: Two byte-identical direct calls ran against one real ledger; their proposal, request, and event rows were enumerated and compared for identity and content.

rows.probe: handle on the same System after a submission: result and durable footprint against the baseline
rows.note: After direct submission on one configured System, unchanged handle ran on the same input; its result, source count, full table delta, and both pending bindings were measured.

rows.probe: read-site census: read-transaction sites, write-transaction sites, reached helpers and violations
rows.note: The production AST was scanned with the gate's recursive connection-flow algorithm, then a real success proved the new read and write sites execute in that order.
